欢迎

Thank you for purchasing the MEAP for Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch).

感谢您购买“从零开始构建推理模型”的MEAP版本。

If you are like most people these days, LLMs are already part of your everyday toolkit. Maybe you have asked an LLM to proofread an email, debug a tricky piece of code, or explain a concept that sent you down an unexpected rabbit hole. Since 2022, and the launch of ChatGPT, these models have moved from experimental novelties to essential tools in our daily work and learning.

如果你和如今的大多数人一样，大型语言模型早已成为你日常工具箱的一部分。也许你曾让大型语言模型帮你校对邮件、调试一段棘手的代码，或是解释一个让你陷入复杂细节的概念。自2022年ChatGPT发布以来，这类模型已经从实验性的新奇事物，转变为我们日常工作和学习中不可或缺的工具。

It’s been quite a journey to get here. The earliest GPT models, introduced in 2018, could generate text that was more or less human-like, but they were primarily text-completion models, largely unable to answer even simple queries, and the response quality was nowhere near that of the LLMs we use today.

走到今天，可谓历经艰辛。最早的GPT模型于2018年问世，能够生成或多或少接近人类写作水平的文本，但它们本质上只是文本补全模型，连简单的提问都难以回答，生成内容的质量也远不及如今我们使用的大型语言模型。

Then came instruction fine-tuning and alignment with human preferences, which ChatGPT popularized in 2022. The techniques behind ChatGPT transformed LLMs into the everyday problem solvers we use today. Currently, we are in the latest phase: developing reasoning models. Reasoning is the ability for an LLM to tackle more complex problems step-by-step.

随后出现了基于人类偏好进行的指令微调与对齐技术，这一技术在2022年被ChatGPT推向普及。ChatGPT背后的一系列方法，将大语言模型转变为我们如今日常使用的问题解决工具。目前，我们正处于最新阶段：构建具备推理能力的模型。所谓推理，是指大语言模型能够分步骤地解决更为复杂的问题。

Reasoning is one of the most exciting and important recent advances in improving LLMs, but it’s also one of the easiest to misunderstand if you only hear the term reasoning and read about it in theory. That’s why this book takes a hands-on approach. We’ll start with a pre-trained base LLM and then add reasoning capabilities ourselves, step by step in code, so you can see exactly how it works.

推理是近年来提升大语言模型性能最为令人振奋且重要的进展之一，但若仅从字面意义或理论层面了解“推理”这一概念，也最容易产生误解。正因如此，本书采取了实践导向的方式。我们将从一个预训练的基础大语言模型入手，然后通过逐行编写代码、逐步添加推理能力，让你直观地看到其工作原理。

This book isn’t a “production deployment” manual, and we won’t use any third-party LLM libraries. Instead, think of it as a behind-the-scenes tour where you get to develop the machinery yourself.

本书并非“生产环境部署”指南，我们也不会使用任何第三方大模型库。相反，你可以把它看作一次幕后之旅——你将亲手打造这套机器。

By the end, you will not only understand what reasoning is and how it works, but you will also have built it from scratch. That’s a perspective that will serve you well whether you are using, developing, or planning to deploy LLMs in the future.

到课程结束时，你不仅会理解什么是推理以及它的工作原理，还将从零开始构建一个推理系统。无论你目前是在使用大语言模型、开发相关技术，还是未来计划部署它们，这种视角都将对你大有裨益。

请务必在 liveBook 讨论区发布您对本书的任何问题、评论或建议。

1 Understanding reasoning models

1 理解推理模型

Welcome to the next stage of large language models (LLMs): reasoning. LLMs have transformed how we process and generate text, but their success has been largely driven by statistical pattern recognition. New advances in reasoning methods now enable LLMs to tackle more complex tasks, such as solving logical puzzles and multi-step math problems.

欢迎来到大型语言模型（LLMs）发展的新阶段——推理。LLMs 已经彻底改变了我们处理和生成文本的方式，但其成功在很大程度上依赖于统计模式识别。如今，推理方法的新进展使 LLMs 能够应对更加复杂的任务，例如解答逻辑谜题和多步数学问题。

Moreover, reasoning is an essential technique for making AI agents practical, for example when an agent has to break a task into steps, use tools, and recover from mistakes. Reasoning LLMs are already used in agent applications such as OpenClaw.

此外，推理是使AI智能体具备实用性的关键技术——例如，当智能体需要将任务分解为多个步骤、使用工具并从错误中恢复时。目前，基于推理的大语言模型已应用于OpenClaw等智能体系统中。

In Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), you will learn the inner workings of LLM reasoning methods through a hands-on, code-first approach. We will start from a pre-trained LLM and extend it step by step with reasoning capabilities. We implement these reasoning components ourselves, from scratch, to see how these methods work in practice.

在《从零构建推理模型》课程中，你将通过实践导向、以代码为核心的教学方式，深入理解大语言模型推理机制的内部运作。我们将从一个预训练的大语言模型出发，逐步为其添加推理能力。所有推理组件都将由我们从头开始自行实现，以便直观地观察这些方法在实际应用中的工作原理。

If you are curious about how LLMs themselves are built and trained, my earlier book Build A Large Language Model (From Scratch) published by Manning (http://mng.bz/orYv) provides a detailed coverage of these foundations, but it is not required for following along here.

如果你想了解大型语言模型究竟是如何构建和训练的，我此前由Manning出版社出版的《从零开始构建大型语言模型》一书（http://mng.bz/orYv）对此进行了详尽的阐述。不过，要理解本书的内容，并不需要先读那本书。

Even with a cursory knowledge of how LLMs are built, you will understand, by the end of this book, how reasoning models work and be equipped to design, prototype, and evaluate the main methods for improving reasoning in LLMs.

即便你对大型语言模型的构建仅有初步了解，读完本书后，你也能够理解推理模型的工作原理，并具备设计、原型开发及评估用于提升大型语言模型推理能力的主要方法的能力。

When working with reasoning models, it’s crucial to know how to check automatically whether those answers are correct on tasks such as math, and how to turn a general-purpose model into a smaller reasoning model.

在使用推理模型时，至关重要的是掌握如何自动检验这些模型在数学等任务上的答案是否正确，以及如何将通用模型转化为规模更小的推理模型。

We will use math examples throughout the book because they are easy to check automatically, but advanced math knowledge is not required to follow along. Understanding reasoning methods is the central focus of this book.

本书将贯穿使用数学例题，因为这些题目易于自动检验，但读者无需具备高等数学知识即可跟上。本书的核心在于理解推理方法。

With its focus on practical applications and explanations, this book is written to speak to LLM engineers, machine learning researchers, applied scientists, and software developers alike. Understanding how reasoning models are set up helps us judge when a standard LLM is sufficient and when extra reasoning machinery is worth the added complexity, cost, and latency. It also helps us design better evaluations, debug failures on multi-step tasks, and adapt reasoning techniques to real products and research workflows.

本书以实用应用和深入阐释为核心，旨在面向大语言模型工程师、机器学习研究人员、应用科学家以及软件开发者。理解推理模型的构建方式，有助于我们判断在何种场景下使用标准的大语言模型即可满足需求，而在何种情况下则需要引入额外的推理机制，以权衡其带来的复杂性、成本和延迟。同时，这也有助于我们设计更完善的评估方法、诊断多步任务中的故障，并将推理技术适配到实际产品和研究工作流中。

1.1 Defining reasoning in the context of LLMs

1.1 在大语言模型语境下对推理的定义

In this book, I use the term reasoning in a practical engineering sense rather than a philosophical one. In the context of LLMs, reasoning refers to a model generating intermediate steps before producing its final answer.

在本书中，我所使用的“推理”一词，是从实用的工程角度出发，而非哲学意义上的。在大语言模型的语境下，推理指的是模型在给出最终答案之前，先生成一系列中间步骤。

These intermediate steps may appear as a visible step-by-step explanation, or they may be enclosed in special tags such as <think>...</think> and hidden from the user. In either case, the core idea remains the same, that is, the model is encouraged or trained to spend tokens on intermediate problem solving instead of jumping directly to the conclusion.

这些中间步骤可以以可见的分步解释形式呈现，也可以用特殊标签（如 <think>…</think>）包裹起来，对用户隐藏。无论采用哪种方式，核心思想都是一致的：鼓励或训练模型在解决问题的过程中逐步消耗上下文 tokens，而不是直接跳到结论。

Correspondingly, I use reasoning model to mean an LLM that has been improved, either through training or prompting techniques, to produce such intermediate steps, which often increases accuracy on complex tasks such as coding, logical puzzles, and math problems.

相应地，我将“推理模型”定义为经过训练或提示技术改进的大型语言模型，使其能够生成这类中间步骤，从而通常在编码、逻辑谜题和数学问题等复杂任务上提高准确性。

Before we get to the coding portions of this book in the upcoming chapters, I will briefly discuss the main techniques that improve these reasoning behaviors and how they relate to pattern matching and logical reasoning. This will lay the groundwork for further discussions on how LLMs are currently built, how they handle reasoning tasks, and what they are good and not so good at.

在接下来的章节中进入本书的编码部分之前，我将简要探讨几种能够提升推理能力的主要技术，以及它们与模式匹配和逻辑推理之间的关系。这将为后续讨论大语言模型的当前构建方式、其如何处理推理任务，以及它们的优势与局限性奠定基础。

Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
思维链（CoT）

This style of intermediate-step generation is often referred to as chain-of-thought (CoT). Researchers and engineers often say that the model "thinks" through the problem step by step, meaning that it makes its intermediate reasoning process explicit and easier to follow. In this book, I use the terms reasoning and thinking in that common engineering sense. This does not imply that LLMs actually reason or think in the same way humans do.

这种生成中间步骤的方式通常被称为“思维链”（CoT）。研究者和工程师常常说，模型会一步步“思考”问题，也就是说，它会将中间推理过程明确地展现出来，从而使得整个推理过程更加清晰易懂。在本书中，我沿用工程领域中的常见用法，将“推理”和“思考”这两个术语作如此理解。这并不意味着大型语言模型真的能够像人类一样进行推理或思考。

Figure 1.1 illustrates how a conventional LLM generates the answer to a user's question.

图1.1展示了传统大型语言模型如何生成用户问题的答案。

Figure 1.1 A simplified illustration of how a conventional, non-reasoning LLM might respond to a question with a short answer.
图1.1 一个简化示意图，展示了传统的、不具备推理能力的语言模型如何对一个问题给出简短答案。

As shown in figure 1.1, a conventional LLM might not show how it came up with its answer. While the answer might be correct it doesn't help the user understand the process behind the answer.

如图1.1所示，传统的大型语言模型可能不会展示其得出答案的过程。尽管答案可能是正确的，但它并不能帮助用户理解答案背后的推理过程。

Figure 1.2 illustrates a simple example of multi-step (CoT) reasoning in an LLM.

图1.2展示了一个大型语言模型中多步（CoT）推理的简单示例。

Figure 1.2 A simplified illustration of how a reasoning LLM might tackle a multi-step reasoning task using a chain-of-thought. Rather than just recalling a fact, the model combines several intermediate reasoning steps to arrive at the correct conclusion. The intermediate reasoning steps may or may not be shown to the user, depending on the implementation.
图1.2 一个简化的示意图，展示了推理型大语言模型如何利用思维链来解决多步推理任务。与单纯回忆事实不同，该模型会结合多个中间推理步骤，最终得出正确结论。这些中间推理步骤是否向用户展示，取决于具体的实现方式。

LLM-produced intermediate reasoning steps, as shown in figure 1.2, look very much like a person articulating internal thoughts aloud. Yet how closely these methods (and the resulting reasoning processes) mirror human reasoning remains an open research question, one this book does not attempt to answer.

如图1.2所示，大语言模型生成的中间推理步骤，看起来非常类似于人类将内心思考清晰地表达出来。然而，这些方法（以及由此产生的推理过程）在多大程度上能够准确模拟人类的推理方式，仍然是一个尚未解决的研究问题，本书并不试图对此作出回答。

While figure 1.2 is a typical example of chain-of-thought reasoning, it is important to emphasize that LLM reasoning differs from traditional, deterministic reasoning.

尽管图1.2是思维链推理的一个典型示例，但需要强调的是，大语言模型的推理与传统的确定性推理存在本质区别。

For instance, a symbolic logic engine or theorem prover follows strict, rule-based steps that guarantee consistency and correctness. A symbolic logic engine works like following a recipe where every step is fixed and must produce the same result each time. To use a cooking analogy, if you follow the steps exactly, you always end up with the same dish.

例如，一个符号逻辑引擎或定理证明器会严格按照基于规则的步骤运行，从而保证一致性和正确性。符号逻辑引擎的工作方式就像按照一份食谱操作一样：每一步都是固定的，每次执行都必须得到相同的结果。用烹饪作比喻，如果你完全按照步骤来操作，最终总会做出同一道菜。

In contrast to a symbolic logic engine, an LLM generates reasoning autoregressively, which means that it is predicting one token at a time based on statistical patterns in its training data. As a result, the LLM's "reasoning steps" are not guaranteed to be logically sound, even if they look convincing.

与符号逻辑引擎不同，大型语言模型是以自回归方式生成推理过程的——也就是说，它会基于训练数据中的统计规律，一次预测一个词元。因此，即使大型语言模型的“推理步骤”看起来颇具说服力，也并不能保证其逻辑上完全正确。

This book focuses on explaining and implementing the fundamental techniques that improve LLM-based reasoning and thus make LLMs better at handling complex tasks. My hope is that by gaining hands-on experience with these methods, you will be better prepared to understand and improve those reasoning methods being developed and maybe even explore how they compare to human reasoning.

本书重点阐释并实践那些能够提升基于大语言模型推理能力的基础技术，从而使大语言模型更擅长处理复杂任务。我的期望是，通过亲自动手实践这些方法，你将更能理解并改进正在研发的各类推理技术，甚至进一步探讨它们与人类推理方式的异同。

LLM versus human reasoning
大语言模型与人类推理

Reasoning processes in LLMs may superficially resemble human thought, particularly in how intermediate steps are articulated. It is important to recognize a key difference: humans can engage in deterministic reasoning by deliberately applying rules of logic or by reasoning over an internal model of the world. Deterministic here means that if we start with the same facts and follow the same steps, we will always reach the same conclusion. In contrast, current LLM reasoning is probabilistic, meaning that it generates one token at a time based on statistical patterns in training data, without guarantees of logical consistency.

大型语言模型中的推理过程在表面上可能与人类思维相似，尤其是在中间步骤的表达方式上。然而，需要认识到一个关键区别：人类可以通过有意识地运用逻辑规则，或基于对世界的内部表征进行推理，来进行确定性推理。所谓“确定性”，是指如果起始事实相同、遵循相同的推理步骤，就一定会得出相同的结论。相比之下，当前的大型语言模型推理则是概率性的，即它根据训练数据中的统计模式逐个生成词元，而无法保证逻辑一致性。

Humans often reason by consciously manipulating concepts, intuitively understanding abstract relationships, or generalizing from a few examples. LLMs, by contrast, work by picking up patterns from huge amounts of text rather than relying on built-in reasoning rules or any kind of conscious thought.

人类通常通过有意识地操纵概念、直觉地理解抽象关系，或从少数例子中进行归纳来推理。与此不同，大型语言模型主要是从海量文本中学习并捕捉模式，而非依赖内置的推理规则或任何形式的意识性思维。

In short, although the outputs of reasoning-enhanced LLMs can appear human-like, the underlying mechanisms differ substantially and remain an active area of exploration.

简而言之，尽管推理增强型大语言模型的输出看似人类化，但其内在机制却存在显著差异，目前仍处于积极探索之中。

1.2 Understanding the standard LLM training pipeline

1.2 理解标准的大语言模型训练流程

Now, let’s briefly summarize how conventional (non-reasoning) LLMs are typically trained so that we can understand where their limitations lie. This background will also help frame our upcoming discussions on the differences between pattern matching and logical reasoning.

现在，让我们简要总结一下传统（非推理型）大语言模型的典型训练方式，以便理解其局限性所在。这些背景知识也有助于为我们接下来讨论模式匹配与逻辑推理之间的区别奠定基础。

Before applying any specific reasoning methodology, conventional LLM training is usually structured into two stages: pre-training and post-training, which are illustrated in figure 1.3.

在应用任何特定的推理方法之前，传统的大型语言模型训练通常分为预训练和后训练两个阶段，如图1.3所示。

Some recent papers also distinguish a mid-training stage between them, for example to continue training a model on code, math, or long-context data, but to keep the terminology simple in this book, I group that stage under pre-training.

一些近期的研究论文还在两者之间区分出一个中间训练阶段，例如在代码、数学或长上下文数据上继续训练模型。不过，为了保持本书术语的简洁，我将这一阶段归入预训练范畴。

Figure 1.3 Overview of a typical LLM training pipeline. The process begins with an initial model initialized with random weights, followed by pre-training on large-scale text data to learn language patterns by predicting the next token. Post-training then refines the model through instruction fine-tuning and preference fine-tuning, which enables the LLM to follow human instructions better and align with human preferences.
图1.3 典型大语言模型训练流水线概览。该流程始于一个以随机权重初始化的初始模型，随后在大规模文本数据上进行预训练，通过预测下一个标记来学习语言模式。之后，通过指令微调和偏好微调进一步优化模型，使大语言模型能够更好地遵循人类指令，并与人类偏好保持一致。

In the pre-training stage of a typical LLM training pipeline, as shown in figure 1.3, LLMs are trained on massive amounts of unlabeled text, often many terabytes of data or trillions of tokens, which includes books, websites, research articles, and many other sources. The pre-training objective (goal) for the LLM is to learn to predict the next word (i.e., token) in these texts.

在典型的大型语言模型训练流程的预训练阶段，如图1.3所示，LLM会在海量的无标签文本上进行训练，这些数据通常多达数TB甚至数万亿个标记，涵盖书籍、网页、科研论文等多种来源。LLM的预训练目标是学会预测这些文本中的下一个词（即标记）。

Words and tokens
词语和标记

A token is a small unit of text that a language model processes. A token can be a full word, part of a word, or even punctuation, depending on how the text is split by a so-called tokenizer.

标记（token）是语言模型处理的最小文本单元。根据所谓的分词器（tokenizer）对文本的切分方式，一个标记可以是一个完整的词、词的一部分，甚至是一个标点符号。

For example, the sentence "An LLM can be useful." might be broken into tokens like "An", " L", "LM", " can", " be", " useful", and "." by a common tokenizer. These tokens are then converted into numerical IDs that the model can ingest.

例如，句子“An LLM can be useful.”可能会被常见的分词器拆分为“An”、“ L”、“LM”、“ can”、“ be”、“ useful”和“.”等标记。随后，这些标记会被转换为模型可以处理的数值ID。

A tokenizer is a component that is not directly part of the LLM itself but is nonetheless a critical component of the LLM text processing and generation pipeline. We will see how tokenization works in practice in the next chapter.

分词器并不是大语言模型本身的一部分，但它却是大语言模型文本处理与生成流水线中至关重要的组件。我们将在下一章中具体了解分词的实际工作原理。

LLMs become highly capable when pre-trained on massive datasets, which typically involves several terabytes of text (equivalent to trillions of tokens). This training requires thousands of GPUs running for many months and can cost millions of dollars. Here, "capable" means that the LLMs begin to generate text that closely resembles human writing. Also, to some extent, pre-trained LLMs will begin to exhibit so-called emergent properties, which means that they will be able to perform tasks that they were not explicitly trained to do, including translation, code generation, and so on.

大型语言模型在大规模数据集上进行预训练后，会具备强大的能力。这些数据集通常包含数TB的文本，相当于数万亿个词元。这样的训练需要数千张GPU卡持续运行数月之久，成本可能高达数百万美元。这里的“能力”指的是，这些模型开始生成与人类写作高度相似的文本。此外，在一定程度上，经过预训练的大型语言模型还会表现出所谓的涌现性，即能够完成那些并未被显式训练过的任务，例如机器翻译、代码生成等。

These pre-trained models merely serve as base models for the post-training stage, which uses two key techniques: supervised fine-tuning (often abbreviated as SFT in the literature and also known as instruction tuning) and preference tuning (often implemented via a technique called Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback) to teach LLMs to respond to user queries, which are illustrated in figure 1.4.

这些预训练模型仅作为后训练阶段的基础模型，该阶段采用两种关键技术：监督微调（在相关文献中常简称为 SFT，亦称指令微调）和偏好微调（通常通过一种称为“人类反馈强化学习”的技术实现），以训练大语言模型响应用户查询，如图 1.4 所示。

Figure 1.4 Example responses from a language model at different training stages. The prompt asks for a summary of the relationship between sleep and health. The pre-trained LLM produces a relevant but unfocused answer without directly following the instructions. The instruction-tuned LLM generates a concise and accurate summary aligned with the prompt. The preference-tuned LLM further improves the response by using a friendly tone and engaging language, which makes the answer more relatable and user-centered.
图1.4 不同训练阶段语言模型的示例回复。提示要求总结睡眠与健康之间的关系。预训练的语言模型给出的回答虽相关，但不够聚焦，未能直接遵循指令。经过指令微调的语言模型生成了一篇简洁准确、与提示高度一致的摘要。而经过偏好微调的语言模型则在此基础上进一步优化了回复，采用亲切友好的语气和富有吸引力的语言，使回答更具共鸣感、更以用户为中心。

As shown in figure 1.4, instruction tuning improves an LLM's capabilities of personal assistance-like tasks such as question-answering, summarizing and translating text, and many more. The preference tuning stage then refines these capabilities. As the term implies, preference tuning helps tailor responses to user preferences. Some readers may be familiar with terms like Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback or RLHF, which are specific techniques to implement preference tuning.

如图1.4所示，指令微调能够提升大型语言模型在个人助理类任务上的能力，例如问答、文本摘要和翻译等，以及更多其他任务。随后的偏好微调阶段则会对这些能力进行进一步优化。顾名思义，偏好微调旨在使模型的响应更加贴合用户的偏好。部分读者可能熟悉“人类反馈强化学习”或RLHF等术语，它们正是实现偏好微调的具体技术方法。

In short, we can think of pre-training as "raw language prediction" (via next-token prediction) that gives the LLM some basic properties and capabilities to produce coherent texts. The post-training stage then improves the task understanding of LLMs via instruction tuning and refines the LLM to create answers with preferred stylistic choices via preference tuning.

简而言之，预训练可以被视为一种“原始语言预测”（通过下一个词预测），它赋予大语言模型一些基本属性和能力，使其能够生成连贯的文本。而后续的微调阶段则通过指令微调提升模型的任务理解能力，并通过偏好微调进一步优化模型，使其生成符合特定风格偏好的回答。

It is worth noting that even an instruction-tuned model is not yet a "chatbot." A chat interface adds another layer that guides the model's responses in an interactive, multi-turn setting. This typically involves a system prompt, conversation history management, and other orchestration (an example of this is implemented in appendix G).

值得注意的是，即便经过指令微调的模型，也还称不上“聊天机器人”。聊天界面在此基础上又增加了一层，能够在交互式、多轮对话的场景中引导模型生成回应。这通常涉及系统提示词、对话历史管理以及其他编排机制（相关示例见附录G）。

NOTE
注意

These pre-training and post-training stages mentioned above are covered in my book "Build A Large Language Model (From Scratch)" (http://mng.bz/orYv) published by Manning. The book you are reading now does not require detailed knowledge of these stages. We will load a model that has already undergone the expensive pre-training and post-training stages mentioned above, so that we can focus on the methodology that is specific to reasoning models in the subsequent chapters.

上述预训练和后训练阶段在我的著作《从零构建大型语言模型》（http://mng.bz/orYv）中有所介绍，该书由Manning出版社出版。而你目前阅读的这本书并不需要对这些阶段有深入的了解。在接下来的内容中，我们将直接加载一个已经完成昂贵的预训练和后训练阶段的模型，以便在后续章节中专注于专属于推理模型的方法论。

1.3 Improving LLM reasoning with training and inference techniques

1.3 通过训练和推理技术提升大语言模型的推理能力

Reasoning in the context of LLMs became popular in the public eye with the announcement of OpenAI's o1 in ChatGPT on September 12, 2024, which popularized the concept of reasoning in LLMs. In the announcement article (https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-o1-preview/), OpenAI mentioned that "We've developed a new series of AI models designed to spend more time thinking before they respond."

大型语言模型中的推理能力，随着OpenAI于2024年9月12日在ChatGPT中宣布推出o1模型而迅速进入公众视野，从而使得“推理”这一概念在LLM领域广为人知。在相关公告文章（https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-o1-preview/）中，OpenAI指出：“我们开发了一系列全新的AI模型，旨在在作出回应之前投入更多时间进行思考。”

Furthermore, OpenAI wrote: "These enhanced reasoning capabilities may be particularly useful if you're tackling complex problems in science, coding, math, and similar fields."

此外，OpenAI 还写道：“这些增强的推理能力在您解决科学、编程、数学及类似领域的复杂问题时，可能会特别有用。”

A few months later, in January 2025, DeepSeek released the DeepSeek-R1 model and technical report (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948), which details training methodologies to develop reasoning models, which made big waves as they not only made freely and openly available a model that competes with and exceeds the performance of the proprietary o1 model but also shared a blueprint on how to train such a model.

几个月后，即2025年1月，DeepSeek发布了DeepSeek-R1模型及技术报告（https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948），详细介绍了用于训练推理模型的方法论。这一发布引发了巨大轰动：DeepSeek不仅免费开放了一个性能可与专有模型o1相媲美甚至超越其表现的模型，还公开了如何训练此类模型的完整方案。

We aim to understand how these methodologies used to develop reasoning models work by implementing similar methods from scratch.

我们旨在通过从头实现类似的方法，来理解用于构建推理模型的各种方法的工作原理。

The different approaches to developing and improving an LLM's reasoning capabilities can be grouped into three broad categories, as illustrated in figure 1.4.

如图1.4所示，用于开发和提升大语言模型推理能力的不同方法可以归纳为三大类。

Figure 1.5 Three approaches commonly used to improve reasoning capabilities in LLMs. These methods (inference-compute scaling, reinforcement learning, and distillation) are typically applied after the conventional training stages (initial model training, pre-training, and post-training with instruction and preference tuning), but reasoning techniques can also be applied to the pre-trained base model.
图1.5 常用于提升大语言模型推理能力的三种方法。这些方法（推理—计算规模扩展、强化学习和知识蒸馏）通常在常规训练阶段（初始模型训练、预训练以及基于指令和偏好微调的后训练）之后应用，但推理技术也可直接应用于预训练的基础模型。

As illustrated in figure 1.5, these methods are typically applied to LLMs that have undergone the conventional pre-training and post-training phases, including instruction and preference tuning. The following list provides a brief introduction to the three common approaches that we will examine in more detail throughout the rest of the book.

如图1.5所示，这些方法通常应用于已经完成传统预训练和后训练阶段的大语言模型，其中包括指令微调和偏好对齐。下文将简要介绍三种常用的方法，我们将在本书后续章节中对其进行更详细的探讨。

  1. Inference-time compute scaling (also often called inference-compute scaling, test-time scaling, or other variations) includes methods that improve model reasoning capabilities at inference time (when a user prompts the model) without training or modifying the underlying model weights. The core idea is to trade off increased computational resources for improved performance, which helps make even fixed models more capable through techniques such as chain-of-thought reasoning, and various sampling procedures. This topic will be the focus of chapters 4 and 5.
  2. 推理时计算扩展（也常称为推理计算扩展、测试时扩展或其他类似术语）是指在不训练或修改模型底层权重的情况下，在推理阶段（即用户向模型提出问题或指令时）提升模型推理能力的一系列方法。其核心思想是通过增加计算资源来换取性能的提升，从而借助诸如思维链推理和各类采样策略等技术，使即使是固定不变的模型也能表现出更强的能力。本主题将作为第4章和第5章的重点内容。
  3. Reinforcement learning (RL) refers to training methods that improve a model's reasoning capabilities by encouraging it to take actions that lead to high reward signals. These rewards can be broad, such as task success or heuristic scores, or they can be narrowly defined and verifiable, such as correct answers in math problems or coding tasks.
  4. 强化学习（RL）是指通过鼓励模型采取能够带来高奖励信号的行为，从而提升其推理能力的训练方法。这些奖励既可以是较为宽泛的，例如任务成功或启发式评分；也可以是定义明确且可验证的，例如数学问题或编程任务中的正确答案。
  5. Unlike Inference-time compute scaling, which can improve reasoning performance without modifying the model, RL updates the model's weights during training. This enables the model to learn and refine reasoning strategies through trial and error, based on the feedback it receives from the environment. We will explore RL in more detail in chapters 6 and 7.
  6. 与推理时的计算规模扩展不同——后者可以在不修改模型的情况下提升推理性能——强化学习会在训练过程中更新模型的权重。这使得模型能够根据从环境中获得的反馈，通过试错来学习并优化推理策略。我们将在第6章和第7章中更详细地探讨强化学习。
  7. Distillation involves transferring complex reasoning patterns learned by strong, larger models into smaller or more efficient models. Within the context of LLMs, this typically means performing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using high-quality labeled instruction datasets generated by a larger, more capable model. This technique is commonly referred to as knowledge distillation or simply distillation in LLM literature. It's important to note that this differs slightly from traditional knowledge distillation in deep learning, where a smaller ("student") model typically learns from both the outputs and the logits produced by a larger ("teacher") model. This topic is discussed further in chapter 8.
  8. 知识蒸馏是指将强大、规模较大的模型所学习到的复杂推理模式迁移到规模较小或效率更高的模型中。在大语言模型的背景下，这通常意味着使用由更大、更强大的模型生成的高质量标注指令数据集，对目标模型进行监督微调（SFT）。这一技术在大语言模型相关文献中通常被称为“知识蒸馏”或简称“蒸馏”。需要注意的是，这与深度学习中的传统知识蒸馏略有不同：在后者中，较小的“学生”模型通常会同时学习来自较大“教师”模型的输出和 logits。关于这一主题的更多讨论将在第8章中展开。
Reinforcement learning for reasoning and preference tuning
用于推理和偏好调整的强化学习

In the context of developing reasoning models, it is important to distinguish the RL approach here from reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF), which is used during preference tuning when developing a conventional LLM as illustrated previously in figure 1.5.

在构建推理模型的背景下，有必要将此处的强化学习方法与基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）区分开来。RLHF主要用于在偏好调优阶段训练传统的大型语言模型，如图1.5所示。

Both settings use the same underlying process (RL) but they differ primarily in how the reward is obtained and validated (human judgments for RLHF versus automated verifiers or environments for reasoning RL).

这两种设置都使用相同的底层机制（强化学习），但它们的主要区别在于奖励的获取和验证方式：RLHF 依赖人类判断，而推理强化学习则依靠自动化验证器或环境。

RLHF incorporates explicit human evaluations or rankings of model outputs as reward signals, directly guiding the model toward human-preferred behaviors. In contrast, RL in the context of reasoning models typically relies on automated or environment-based reward signals, which can be more objective but potentially less aligned with human preferences. For instance, RL in a reasoning model development pipeline might train a model to excel at mathematical proofs by providing explicit rewards for correctness. In contrast, RLHF would involve human evaluators ranking various responses to encourage outputs that align closely with human standards and subjective preferences.

RLHF 将人类对模型输出的显式评价或排序作为奖励信号，直接引导模型生成更符合人类偏好的行为。相比之下，在推理模型的强化学习场景中，通常依赖于自动化的或基于环境的奖励信号。这类奖励虽然更为客观，但可能与人类偏好存在一定偏差。例如，在推理模型的开发流程中，强化学习可以通过对正确性给予显式奖励，来训练模型擅长数学证明。而 RLHF 则会由人类评估者对不同响应进行排序，以鼓励模型生成更贴近人类标准和主观偏好的输出。

1.4 Pattern matching versus logical reasoning

1.4 模式匹配与逻辑推理

As mentioned in the previous section, during pre-training, LLMs are exposed to vast quantities of text and learn to predict the next token by identifying and reproducing statistical associations in that data. This process enables them to generate fluent and coherent text, but it is fundamentally based on learned statistical regularities rather than explicit rules or guaranteed logical inference.

如前一节所述，在预训练阶段，大型语言模型会接触海量文本，并通过识别和重现这些数据中的统计关联来学习预测下一个标记。这一过程使它们能够生成流畅且连贯的文本，但其根本原理是基于所习得的统计规律，而非明确的规则或有保证的逻辑推理。

LLMs respond to prompts by generating text continuations that are statistically consistent with the patterns seen during training. This includes many premise-to-conclusion patterns that can look like logical inference. The key difference is that the model does not explicitly represent premises and apply formal rules, but instead predicts likely continuations from similar examples in its training data.

大型语言模型通过生成在统计上与训练期间所见模式一致的文本续写来响应提示。这其中包括许多从前提到结论的模式，这些模式看起来很像逻辑推理。关键区别在于，模型并不会显式地表征前提并应用形式化规则，而是根据其训练数据中的相似实例预测可能的续写。

Consider the following example:

考虑以下示例：

SRPrompt

The capital of Germany is…

德国的首都是……

Response

Berlin.

柏林。

An LLM producing the answer "Berlin" is not logically deducing the answer. Instead, it is recalling a strong statistical association learned from training data. This behavior reflects what we refer to as pattern matching, which means that the model completes text based on learned correlations and not by applying structured reasoning steps.

一个大语言模型给出“柏林”作为答案，并不是通过逻辑推理得出的结论，而是在回忆训练数据中学习到的强统计关联。这种行为体现了我们所说的模式匹配：模型是根据已学习到的文本相关性来完成生成，而非通过执行结构化的推理步骤。

But what about tasks that go beyond pattern recognition, i.e., tasks where a correct answer depends on drawing conclusions from given facts? This brings us to a different kind of capability: logical reasoning.

然而，那些超越模式识别的任务又当如何呢？也就是说，当正确答案取决于从已知事实中得出推理结论时，情况又会怎样？这就引出了另一类能力：逻辑推理。

Logical reasoning involves systematically coming up with conclusions using rules. Unlike pattern matching, it depends on intermediate reasoning steps and the ability to recognize contradictions or draw implications based on formal relationships.

逻辑推理是指运用规则系统地得出结论的过程。与模式匹配不同，它依赖于中间的推理步骤，以及识别矛盾或基于形式化关系推导出结论的能力。

Consider the following prompt as an example:

以以下提示为例：

  • Prompt: "All birds can fly. A penguin is a bird. Can a penguin fly?"
  • 提示：所有的鸟都会飞。企鹅是一种鸟。那么，企鹅会飞吗？

There are two ways to evaluate this.

有两种方法可以评估这一点。

First, in a closed-world (prompt only) setting, from the two premises (claims, assumptions) in the prompt ("All birds can fly" and "A penguin is a bird"), the valid answer is "Yes, a penguin can fly."

首先，在封闭世界（仅依据题干）的设定下，根据题干中的两个前提（陈述、假设）——“所有的鸟都会飞”和“企鹅是鸟”——有效的答案是：“是的，企鹅会飞。”

Second, in an open-world (with background knowledge) setting, if we also allow background knowledge not included in the prompt (for example, that penguins cannot fly), this external fact conflicts with the conclusion derived from the premises, as shown in figure 1.6. A reasoning system should notice the inconsistency and either ask for clarification or weaken the first statement (for example, "Most birds can fly, with exceptions such as penguins").

其次，在开放世界（具备背景知识）的情境下，如果我们允许使用提示中未包含的背景知识（例如，企鹅不会飞），那么这一外部事实就会与由前提推导出的结论相冲突，如图1.6所示。推理系统应当察觉到这种不一致，并采取相应措施：要么请求进一步澄清，要么弱化第一句话的表述（例如，“大多数鸟类都能飞行，但也有例外，比如企鹅”）。

Figure 1.6 Contradictory premises lead to a logical inconsistency. From "All birds can fly" and "A penguin is a bird," we infer "Penguin can fly." This conclusion conflicts with the established fact "Penguin cannot fly," which results in a contradiction.
图1.6 矛盾的前提会导致逻辑矛盾。由“所有鸟都会飞”和“企鹅是鸟”这两条前提，我们可以推导出“企鹅会飞”。然而，这一结论与已知事实“企鹅不会飞”相冲突，从而产生矛盾。

Figure 1.6 shows how a system based on logical reasoning could process the previously introduced "All birds can fly..." prompt.

图1.6展示了基于逻辑推理的系统如何处理之前提到的“所有的鸟都会飞……”这一提示。

In contrast, a statistical (pattern-matching) LLM does not explicitly track contradictions, such as the one shown in figure 1.6, but instead predicts based on learned text distributions. For instance, if information such as "All birds can fly" is reinforced strongly in training data, the model may confidently answer: "Yes, penguins can fly."

相比之下，基于统计（模式匹配）的大型语言模型并不会显式地追踪矛盾——例如图1.6所示的矛盾——而是根据其从训练数据中学习到的文本分布来进行预测。例如，如果训练数据中反复强化“所有鸟类都会飞”这一信息，那么该模型很可能会自信地回答：“是的，企鹅会飞。”

In the next section, we will look at a concrete example of how an LLM handles this "All birds can fly..." prompt.

在下一节中，我们将探讨一个具体示例，说明大型语言模型如何处理“所有的鸟都会飞……”这一提示。

Logical reasoning and rule-based systems
逻辑推理与基于规则的系统

Why are explicit rule-based systems not more popular? Rule-based systems were used widely in the '80s and '90s for medical diagnosis, legal decisions, and engineering. They are still used in critical domains (medicine, law, aerospace), which often require explicit inference and transparent decision processes. They are hard to implement as they largely rely on human-crafted heuristics. (Heuristics are simple decision rules that give a good-enough answer quickly without guaranteeing an optimal one.) In contrast, deep neural networks, including LLMs, do not implement hand-written rules; they learn decision patterns from data and can be highly flexible when trained at scale.

为什么显式规则系统并不更加流行呢？在20世纪80年代和90年代，规则系统曾广泛应用于医学诊断、法律决策和工程领域。时至今日，它们仍在一些关键领域（如医疗、法律、航空航天）中使用，因为这些领域往往需要明确的推理过程和透明的决策机制。然而，规则系统的实现难度较大，因为它在很大程度上依赖于人工编写的启发式规则。所谓启发式规则，就是一种简单的决策准则，能够在不保证最优解的情况下快速给出一个“足够好”的答案。相比之下，深度神经网络（包括大型语言模型）并不采用手工编写的规则；它们从数据中学习决策模式，并且在大规模训练下具有极高的灵活性。

1.5 Simulating reasoning without explicit rules

1.5 无需显式规则的推理模拟

We saw how contradictory premises can lead to logical inconsistencies. A conventional LLM does not explicitly track contradictions but generates responses based on learned text distributions.

我们已经看到，相互矛盾的前提会导致逻辑不一致。传统的大型语言模型并不会显式地检测矛盾，而是根据其训练过程中习得的文本分布来生成响应。

Let's see a concrete example, shown in figure 1.7, of how a non-reasoning-enhanced LLM like GPT-4o in OpenAI's ChatGPT responds to the "All birds can fly..." prompt discussed in the previous section.

我们来看一个具体的例子，如图1.7所示，它展示了像OpenAI的ChatGPT中的GPT-4o这样未经过推理增强的大语言模型，是如何回应上一节讨论过的“所有的鸟都会飞……”这一提示的。

Figure 1.7 An illustrative example of how a language model (GPT-4o in ChatGPT) appears to "reason" about a contradictory premise.
图1.7 语言模型（在ChatGPT中为GPT-4o）似乎如何对自相矛盾的前提进行“推理”的示例。

The example in figure 1.7 shows that GPT-4o appears to answer correctly even though this model is not considered a reasoning model, unlike OpenAI's other offerings like o1, o3, o4-mini, and more recent GPT-5, which have been explicitly developed with reasoning methodology.

图1.7中的示例表明，GPT-4o即便并非推理型模型——与OpenAI的其他产品如o1、o3、o4-mini以及更近期的GPT-5不同，那些模型都是基于明确的推理方法论开发的——仍能给出正确答案。

So, how did the 4o model generate its answer? Does this mean GPT-4o explicitly reasons logically? No, not necessarily. At a minimum 4o is highly effective at simulating logical reasoning in familiar contexts.

那么，4o 模型是如何得出其答案的呢？这是否意味着 GPT-4o 会明确地进行逻辑推理？并不一定。至少可以肯定的是，4o 在熟悉的情境中能够非常有效地模拟逻辑推理过程。

GPT-4o does not implement explicit contradiction-checking and instead generates answers based on probability-weighted patterns. This approach works well enough if training data includes many instances correcting the contradiction (e.g., text like "penguins cannot fly") so that the model learns a statistical association between "penguins" and "not flying." As we see in figure 1.7, this allows the model to answer correctly without explicitly implementing rule-based or explicit logical reasoning methodologies.

GPT-4o 并未实现显式的矛盾检测机制，而是基于概率加权的模式生成答案。如果训练数据中包含大量纠正矛盾的实例（例如“企鹅不会飞”这样的文本），使得模型能够学习到“企鹅”与“不会飞”之间的统计关联，那么这种做法就能很好地发挥作用。正如图 1.7 所示，这使模型能够在不显式采用基于规则或明确逻辑推理方法的情况下，给出正确的回答。

In other words, the model recognizes the contradiction implicitly because it has frequently encountered this exact reasoning scenario during training. This effectiveness relies heavily on statistical associations built from a lot of exposure to reasoning-like patterns in training data.

换句话说，该模型之所以能够隐式地识别出矛盾，是因为在训练过程中它频繁遇到完全相同的推理场景。这种有效性在很大程度上依赖于训练数据中大量类似推理模式所构建的统计关联。

So, even when a conventional LLM seems to perform logical deduction as shown in figure 1.7, it's not executing explicit, rule-based logic but is instead leveraging patterns from its vast training data.

因此，即使传统的大型语言模型看似如图1.7所示那样进行逻辑推理，它其实并不是在执行明确的、基于规则的逻辑，而是在利用其海量训练数据中的模式。

Nonetheless, GPT-4o's success here is a great illustration of how powerful implicit pattern matching can become when trained at a massive scale. These types of pattern-based reasoning models usually struggle in scenarios where:

尽管如此，GPT-4o 在这里的出色表现很好地说明了，在大规模训练下，隐式模式匹配能力可以变得多么强大。这类基于模式的推理模型通常在以下场景中表现不佳：

  • The logical scenario is novel (not previously encountered in training data).
  • 该逻辑场景是新颖的（在训练数据中未曾出现过）。
  • Reasoning complexity is high, involving intricate, multi-step logical relationships.
  • 推理复杂度较高，涉及错综复杂、多步骤的逻辑关系。
Logical reasoning and current reasoning LLM offerings
逻辑推理与当前的推理大模型产品

While GPT-4o is not officially labeled as a reasoning model, OpenAI offers several dedicated reasoning models, including o1, o3, o4-mini, and GPT-5. Moreover, other companies have been developing LLMs with explicit reasoning capabilities. As of this writing, popular examples include Anthropic's Claude 4, xAI's Grok 4, Google's Gemini 2.5, DeepSeek's R1, Alibaba's Qwen3, and many more. The techniques employed by these models are the focus of this book. As we will see, this is achieved without implementing a rule-based reasoning pipeline (figure 1.6 illustrates the general idea of rule-based reasoning). Instead, the LLM learns or improves its reasoning capabilities as a result of the modified inference and training methodologies.

尽管GPT-4o并未被官方归类为推理模型，但OpenAI仍推出了多款专门的推理模型，包括o1、o3、o4-mini以及GPT-5。此外，其他公司也在积极研发具备明确推理能力的大语言模型。截至本文撰写时，较为流行的实例包括Anthropic的Claude 4、xAI的Grok 4、谷歌的Gemini 2.5、DeepSeek的R1、阿里巴巴的Qwen3等。这些模型所采用的技术正是本书探讨的重点。正如我们将在后续内容中看到的那样，实现这一目标并不依赖于基于规则的推理流程（图1.6展示了基于规则推理的基本思路）。相反，大语言模型是通过改进其推理与训练方法，从而自主学习或提升自身的推理能力。

We might say that LLMs simulate logical reasoning through learned patterns, and we can improve it further with specific reasoning methods that include inference-compute scaling and post-training strategies like reinforcement learning, but they are not explicitly executing any rule-based logic internally.

我们可以说，大语言模型通过学习到的模式来模拟逻辑推理；借助推理与计算规模扩展、强化学习等后训练策略等特定推理方法，还可以进一步提升其推理能力。然而，这些模型内部并未显式地执行任何基于规则的逻辑。

Moreover, it's worth mentioning that reasoning in LLMs exists on a spectrum. This means that even before the advent of dedicated reasoning models such as OpenAI's o1 and DeepSeek-R1, LLMs were capable of simulating reasoning behavior. For instance, these models exhibited behaviors aligning with our earlier definition, such as generating intermediate steps to arrive at correct conclusions. What we now explicitly label a "reasoning model" is essentially a more refined version of this capability. And these improved reasoning capabilities are achieved by leveraging specific inference-compute scaling techniques (chapters 4 and 5) and targeted post-training methods, such as reinforcement learning (chapters 6 and 7), which are designed to improve and reinforce reasoning-like behavior.

此外，值得一提的是，大语言模型中的推理能力实际上处于一个连续谱上。这意味着，即便在专门的推理模型——如OpenAI的o1和DeepSeek-R1——出现之前，大语言模型就已经能够模拟推理行为。例如，这些模型会表现出与我们先前定义相符的行为，比如生成中间步骤以得出正确结论。如今我们明确称为“推理模型”的，本质上只是这一能力的进一步优化版本。而这些增强的推理能力，正是通过运用特定的推理—计算规模扩展技术（第4章和第5章）以及有针对性的后训练方法——如强化学习（第6章和第7章）——来实现的，这些方法旨在提升并强化类似推理的行为。

1.6 Why build reasoning models from scratch?

1.6 为什么要从头构建推理模型？

Following the release of DeepSeek-R1 in January 2025, improving the reasoning abilities of LLMs has become one of the hottest topics in AI, and for good reason. Stronger reasoning skills allow LLMs to tackle more complex problems, making them more capable across various tasks users care about.

2025年1月，DeepSeek-R1发布之后，提升大语言模型的推理能力便成为人工智能领域最热门的话题之一，这并非偶然。更强的推理能力使大语言模型能够应对更加复杂的问题，在用户关注的各类任务中表现得更为出色。

This shift is also reflected in a February 12, 2025, statement from OpenAI's CEO:

这一转变也体现在2025年2月12日OpenAI首席执行官发布的一份声明中：

"We will next ship GPT-4.5, the model we called Orion internally, as our last non-chain-of-thought model. After that, a top goal for us is to unify o-series models and GPT-series models by creating systems that can use all our tools, know when to think for a long time or not, and generally be useful for a very wide range of tasks."
“接下来，我们将推出GPT-4.5——我们在内部称之为‘Orion’的模型——这将是我们最后一款非思维链架构的模型。此后，我们的首要目标之一是通过构建能够综合利用我们所有工具、懂得何时需要长时间思考、何时无需如此，并且在极其广泛的任务中都具有实用价值的系统，来实现O系列模型与GPT系列模型的统一。”

The quote above underlines the major shift from leading LLM providers towards reasoning models, where "chain-of-thought" refers to a prompting technique that guides language models to reason step-by-step to improve their reasoning capabilities, which we will cover in more detail in chapters 4 and 5.

上述引文强调了大型语言模型提供商正在发生的重大转变，即从通用模型向推理模型的转型。“思维链”是一种提示技术，通过引导语言模型按步骤进行推理，以提升其推理能力。我们将在第4章和第5章中对此作更为详细的探讨。

Also noteworthy is the mention of knowing "when to think for a long time or not." This hints at an important design consideration: reasoning is not always necessary or desirable.

同样值得注意的是，文中提到要懂得“何时需要长时间思考，何时则不必”。这暗示了一个重要的设计考量：推理并非总是必要或可取的。

For instance, reasoning models are designed to be good at complex tasks such as solving puzzles, advanced math problems, and challenging coding tasks. They are also often useful in agent systems, especially for task decomposition, planning, and choosing which tools to use. They are not necessary for simpler tasks like summarization, translation, or knowledge-based question answering. In fact, using reasoning models for everything can be inefficient and expensive. For instance, reasoning models are typically more expensive to use, more verbose, and sometimes more prone to errors due to "overthinking." Also, here, the simple rule applies: use the right tool (or type of LLM) for the task.

例如，推理模型擅长处理复杂任务，如解谜、求解高等数学问题以及应对高难度编程挑战。它们在智能体系统中也颇为有用，尤其适用于任务分解、规划以及选择合适的工具。然而，对于摘要生成、机器翻译或基于知识的问答等较为简单的任务，推理模型并非必需。事实上，对所有任务都使用推理模型反而可能效率低下、成本高昂。这是因为推理模型通常调用成本更高、输出更冗长，有时还容易因“过度思考”而产生错误。因此，这里有一条简单原则：针对不同任务选用合适的工具（或相应类型的大型语言模型）。

Reasoning models are often more expensive than non-reasoning models for two reasons.

推理模型通常比非推理模型更昂贵，主要有两个原因。

First, they tend to produce longer outputs because they include intermediate steps that explain how an answer is derived. As figure 1.8 illustrates, LLMs generate text one token at a time and each token requires a full forward pass. If a reasoning model's answer is twice as long, generation involves roughly twice as many forward passes, which increases compute costs.

首先，它们往往生成更长的输出，因为会包含解释答案推导过程的中间步骤。如图1.8所示，大型语言模型每次生成一个词元，而每个词元都需要进行一次完整的前向传播。如果推理模型的答案长度是原来的两倍，则生成过程中所需的前向传播次数也大致增加一倍，从而导致计算成本上升。

Figure 1.8 Token-by-token generation in an LLM. At each step, the LLM takes the full sequence generated so far and predicts the next token, which may represent a word, subword, or punctuation mark depending on the tokenizer. The newly generated token is appended to the sequence and used as input for the next step. This iterative decoding process is used in both standard language models and reasoning-focused models.
图1.8 大型语言模型的逐标记生成过程。在每一步，模型都会接收迄今为止生成的完整序列，并预测下一个标记——该标记可以是词、子词或标点符号，具体取决于分词器的定义。新生成的标记会被追加到序列中，并作为下一步的输入。这种迭代式的解码过程既适用于标准的语言模型，也适用于以推理为重点的模型。

Second, many reasoning workflows require running the model several times for a single task, for example to sample multiple candidate solutions, call tools, or run a verifier. These additional calls multiply the total number of tokens processed and further increase cost beyond the single-call behavior shown in figure 1.8.

其次，许多推理工作流需要针对单个任务多次调用模型，例如采样多个候选解决方案、调用工具或运行验证器。这些额外的调用会成倍增加处理的总 token 数量，并使成本进一步高于图 1.8 所示的单次调用情况。

That's exactly why it helps to implement these models and methods from scratch. It's one of the best ways to understand how they work. And if we understand how LLMs and these reasoning models work, we can better understand these trade-offs.

这正是为什么从头实现这些模型和方法大有裨益的原因。这是理解它们工作原理的最佳途径之一。而一旦我们弄清大型语言模型以及这类推理模型的工作机制，就能更好地把握其中的权衡取舍。

1.7 A roadmap to reasoning models from scratch

1.7 从零开始构建推理模型的路线图

Now that we have discussed reasoning in LLMs from a bird's-eye view, the subsequent chapters will guide you through the process of coding and applying reasoning methods from scratch. At a high level, the roadmap is simple. We start from a conventional LLM, learn how to evaluate its reasoning behavior, and then explore two broad ways to improve it, inference techniques and training techniques. Figure 1.9 summarizes the main steps.

既然我们已经从宏观视角探讨了大语言模型中的推理能力，接下来的几章将引导你从零开始编码并应用各种推理方法。总体而言，我们的路线图非常清晰：我们从一个常规的大语言模型入手，学习如何评估其推理行为，随后深入探索两种主要的改进途径——推理技术与训练技术。图1.9概括了这些主要步骤。

Figure 1.9. A high-level roadmap of what we build in this book. We start with a conventional LLM, add evaluation methods so that we can measure progress, and then explore two broad families of reasoning improvements, namely, inference techniques and training techniques.
图1.9 我们在本书中构建内容的高层次路线图。我们从一个传统的大语言模型入手，加入评估方法以衡量进展，随后探讨两大类推理改进方法：推理技术和训练技术。

Stage 1 is an explicit step in figure 1.9 because, in practice, reasoning methods are usually applied to an existing base LLM rather than trained from scratch. So, we begin with a conventional LLM that has already been pre-trained, and we treat it as the baseline we want to improve.

阶段1在图1.9中被明确列出，这是因为实践中，推理方法通常应用于现有的基础大语言模型，而非从零开始训练。因此，我们从一个已经完成预训练的传统大语言模型入手，并将其视为需要改进的基准模型。

Stage 2 then implements the evaluation tools needed to tell whether a method actually helps. That is why stages 3 and 4 loop back to evaluation, since after improving reasoning behavior through inference-time methods or additional training, we return to stage 2 to measure whether the change actually helped.

第二阶段则实施必要的评估工具，以判断某种方法是否确实有效。这就是为什么第三和第四阶段会回溯到评估环节：在通过推理时方法或额外训练改进推理行为后，我们需要回到第二阶段，衡量这些改进是否真正起到了作用。

Stage 3 improves reasoning behavior at inference time without changing the model weights, while stage 4 improves the model itself through additional training and turns the pre-trained LLM into a dedicated reasoning model.

第三阶段在不改变模型权重的情况下，提升推理时的推理行为；而第四阶段则通过进一步训练来改进模型本身，将预训练的大语言模型转变为专门的推理模型。

Figure 1.10 adds more details and summarizes the different substeps covered in each chapter.

图1.10增加了更多细节，并总结了每一章涵盖的不同子步骤。

Figure 1.10 A detailed roadmap of the chapter-level substeps. After loading the base model, we cover benchmark-based and judgment-based evaluation, then inference-time methods such as advanced text generation and voting plus self-refinement, and finally training-time methods based on reinforcement learning and distillation.
图1.10 章节级子步骤的详细路线图。在加载基础模型之后，我们依次介绍基于基准的评估和基于人类判断的评估，随后是推理时方法，如高级文本生成、投票机制与自我精炼，最后是基于强化学习和知识蒸馏的训练时方法。

As summarized by figure 1.10, chapter 2 introduces the base model, chapter 3 establishes the evaluation methods, chapters 4 and 5 cover the two inference-time techniques, and chapters 6 to 8 cover two training-time techniques.

如图1.10所示，第2章介绍基础模型，第3章建立评估方法，第4章和第5章分别阐述两种推理时技术，而第6至8章则分别讨论两种训练时技术。

I am looking forward to the journey ahead and hope you are as well.

我期待着未来的旅程，也希望你同样充满期待。

1.8 Summary

1.8 总结

  • Conventional LLM training occurs in several stages:
    • Pre-training, where the model learns language patterns from vast amounts of text.
    • 预训练，即模型从海量文本中学习语言模式的过程。
    • Instruction fine-tuning, which improves the model's responses to user prompts.
    • 指令微调，能够提升模型对用户提示的响应质量。
    • Preference tuning, which aligns model outputs with human preferences.
    • 偏好调优，旨在使模型输出与人类偏好保持一致。
  • Reasoning methods are applied on top of a conventional LLM.
  • 推理方法被应用于传统的大型语言模型之上。
  • Reasoning in LLMs refers to improving a model so that it explicitly generates intermediate steps (chain-of-thought) before producing a final answer, which often increases accuracy on multi-step tasks.
  • 大语言模型中的推理是指通过改进模型，使其在给出最终答案之前显式地生成中间步骤（思维链），这通常能够提高多步任务的准确性。
  • Reasoning in LLMs is different from rule-based reasoning and it also likely works differently than human reasoning; currently, the common consensus is that reasoning in LLMs relies on statistical pattern matching.
  • 大语言模型中的推理不同于基于规则的推理，其工作机制也可能与人类的推理方式有所不同。目前学界普遍认为，大语言模型的推理主要依赖于统计模式匹配。
  • Pattern matching in LLMs relies purely on statistical associations learned from data, which enables fluent text generation but lacks explicit logical inference.
  • 大语言模型中的模式匹配完全依赖于从数据中学习到的统计关联，这使得模型能够生成流畅的文本，但却缺乏明确的逻辑推理能力。
  • Improving reasoning in LLMs can be achieved through:
    • Inference-time compute scaling, enhancing reasoning without retraining (e.g., chain-of-thought prompting).
    • 推理时的计算规模扩展，在无需重新训练的情况下提升推理能力（例如，思维链提示）。
    • Reinforcement learning, training models explicitly with reward signals.
    • 强化学习，通过奖励信号显式地训练模型。
    • Supervised fine-tuning and distillation, using examples from stronger reasoning models.
    • 有监督微调与知识蒸馏，以更强推理能力的模型为例。
  • Building reasoning models from scratch provides practical insights into LLM capabilities, limitations, and computational trade-offs.
  • 从头构建推理模型能够为大型语言模型的能力、局限性及计算权衡提供切实的洞见。

2 Generating text with a pre-trained LLM

2 使用预训练的语言模型生成文本

This chapter covers

本章涵盖

  • Setting up the code environment for working with LLMs
  • 搭建用于处理大语言模型的代码环境
  • Using a tokenizer to prepare input text for an LLM
  • 使用分词器为大语言模型准备输入文本
  • The step-by-step process of text generation using a pre-trained LLM
  • 使用预训练大语言模型进行文本生成的逐步过程
  • Caching and compilation techniques for speeding up LLM text generation
  • 用于加速大语言模型文本生成的缓存与编译技术

In the previous chapter, we discussed the difference between conventional large language models (LLMs) and reasoning models. Also, we introduced several techniques to improve the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. These reasoning techniques are usually applied on top of a conventional (base) LLM.

在上一章中，我们讨论了传统大型语言模型（LLMs）与推理模型之间的区别，并介绍了几种用于提升LLMs推理能力的技术。这些推理技术通常被应用于传统的（基础）LLM之上。

In this chapter, we will lay the groundwork for the upcoming chapters by loading a pre-trained base model, as illustrated in figure 2.1. Previously, we discussed how reasoning methods are often added after the usual post-training stages. However, starting from a base model makes it easier to see which capabilities come from the reasoning methods themselves. In other words, the conventional LLM in this chapter is a non-reasoning LLM, and more specifically a pre-trained base model rather than an instruction- or preference-tuned assistant.

在本章中，我们将通过加载一个预训练的基础模型来为后续章节奠定基础，如图2.1所示。此前我们讨论过，推理方法通常是在常规的后训练阶段之后才被引入的。然而，从一个基础模型入手，能够更清晰地辨明哪些能力源自推理方法本身。换言之，本章所提及的传统大语言模型是一个不具备推理能力的语言模型，更具体地说，它是一个预训练的基础模型，而非经过指令微调或偏好微调的助手模型。

Figure 2.1 A mental model depicting the four main stages of developing a reasoning model. This chapter focuses on stage 1, loading a conventional LLM and implementing the text generation functionality.
图2.1 一个心智模型，展示了构建推理模型的四个主要阶段。本章重点讨论第1阶段：加载传统的大型语言模型并实现文本生成功能。

In addition to setting up the coding environment and loading a pre-trained LLM, you will learn how to use a tokenizer to prepare text input for the model. As illustrated in figure 2.1, you will also implement a text generation function, enabling practical use of the LLM to generate text. This functionality will be used and further improved in later chapters.

除了搭建编码环境和加载预训练的大语言模型外，你还将学习如何使用分词器来准备模型所需的文本输入。如图2.1所示，你还将实现一个文本生成函数，从而能够实际运用该大语言模型生成文本。这一功能将在后续章节中被进一步使用和优化。

2.1 Introduction to LLMs for text generation

2.1 用于文本生成的大型语言模型简介

In this chapter, we implement all the necessary LLM essentials, from setting up our coding environment and loading a pre-trained LLM to generating text that we will reuse and build upon in this book. In this sense, this chapter can be understood as a setup chapter.

Even though the LLM is a base model that has only undergone pre-training, it will already be capable of generating coherent text and, in some cases, following basic instructions, as illustrated in figure 2.2.

尽管该大语言模型只是一个仅经过预训练的基础模型，但它已经能够生成连贯的文本，并在某些情况下遵循基本指令，如图2.2所示。

If you have not coded an LLM or used LLMs programmatically before, this chapter will teach you how the text generation process works. In this chapter, we will not go deep into the internals of an LLM, such as the attention mechanism and other architecture components; this is the topic of my other book, Build a Large Language Model (from Scratch). This chapter will also be helpful if you have already read the earlier Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch) book, since it adds new material on speeding up inference and other practical optimizations.

如果你已经读过之前的《从零开始构建大型语言模型》一书，本章同样会对你有所帮助，因为它新增了关于加速推理及其他实用优化的内容。

Before we begin implementing the components shown in figure 2.2, including input preparation, loading the LLM, and generating text, we first need to set up our coding environment. This is the focus of the next section.

2.2 搭建编码环境

This section describes two main ways to set up your Python coding environment to follow along with the examples in this book: a straightforward pip-based setup and a uv-based workflow. I recommend reading this section in its entirety before deciding which option is best for you.

本节介绍了两种主要的 Python 编程环境搭建方式，以便读者能够跟随本书中的示例进行学习：一种是简单的基于 pip 的设置，另一种则是基于 uv 的工作流。建议在决定选择哪种方案之前，先通读本节内容。

If you are reading this book, you have probably coded in Python before. In this case, the simplest way to install dependencies, if you already have a Python environment set up (with Python 3.10 or newer), is to use Python's package installer (pip) in your terminal.

  • torch refers to PyTorch, a widely used deep learning library that provides tools for building and training neural networks.

While pip is the canonical way to install Python packages, my preferred way to use Python is via the widely recommended uv Python package and project manager instead. Like many others, I now recommend uv because it is significantly faster, and it handles dependency resolution more reliably than pip. It also creates isolated environments automatically and comes with its own Python executable (but will use the system Python if a compatible version is already installed) so it is also a great option if you do not have Python installed on your system yet.

虽然 pip 是安装 Python 包的官方标准方式，但我更倾向于使用广受推荐的 uv 工具——它既是一个 Python 包管理器，也是一个项目管理工具。和许多人一样，我如今也推荐使用 uv，因为它速度显著更快，依赖解析也比 pip 更加可靠。此外，uv 还能自动创建隔离的虚拟环境，并自带一个独立的 Python 解释器（当然，如果系统中已安装兼容版本的 Python，它也会直接使用系统自带的 Python）。因此，如果你的系统尚未安装 Python，uv 也是一个非常不错的选择。

2.3 Understanding hardware needs and recommendations

2.3 理解硬件需求和建议

You may have heard that training LLMs is very expensive. For leading LLM companies, it is not uncommon to spend anywhere between 1-10 million dollars on the small end and over 50 million dollars on the high end in terms of compute costs to train a new base model LLM before even adding any reasoning techniques.

你可能听说过，训练大语言模型成本极高。对于行业领先的LLM公司而言，在尚未引入任何推理技术之前，仅训练一个基础模型，计算资源成本就可能低至100万美元、高至5000万美元以上，这并不罕见。

For example, the DeepSeek V3 model, which serves as the base checkpoint for the DeepSeek R1 reasoning system, was trained on 2,048 Nvidia H800 GPUs for about 11 weeks with an estimated cost of 5.5 million USD. (DeepSeek V3 is one of the few more recent models with a fully transparent compute disclosure.)

例如，作为 DeepSeek R1 推理系统基础检查点的 DeepSeek V3 模型，是在 2,048 张 Nvidia H800 GPU 上训练了约 11 周，预计耗资 550 万美元。（DeepSeek V3 是为数不多的、完全公开计算资源投入情况的较新模型之一。）

Furthermore, according to the technical report, the final training run used 14.8 million GPU-hours of compute. The energy usage was roughly 620 MWh, which is roughly the amount of electricity that an average American household uses in about 55 years.

此外，根据技术报告，最终的训练运行共消耗了1480万GPU小时的算力。其能耗约为620兆瓦时，大致相当于一个美国普通家庭约55年间的用电量。

This resource requirements and high price tag would make the development of an LLM unfeasible for me and most readers. So, we are going to use a relatively small (but capable) pre-trained LLM on top of which we implement reasoning techniques.

这样的资源需求和高昂的成本使得开发大型语言模型对我以及大多数读者来说都不现实。因此，我们将使用一个相对较小（但功能强大）的预训练语言模型，并在其基础上实现推理技术。

Note that this smaller LLM is a scaled-down version that otherwise follows the same architecture as contemporary state-of-the-art models. And the reasoning methods that we will apply are the same as those used by larger LLMs. The difference is that the smaller LLM allows us to explore these methods in a budget-friendly way.

需要注意的是，这款规模较小的LLM是当前最先进模型架构的精简版。我们将采用的推理方法也与大型LLM所用的方法相同。不同之处在于，这款小型LLM让我们能够以更为经济的方式探索这些方法。

As an analogy, imagine you are curious to learn how cars work. If you are new to cars, as a learning exercise, you probably wouldn't start out building an expensive Ferrari right away. Instead, you would, for example, create a smaller car like a Volkswagen Beetle to start with, which still teaches you a lot about how engines and the transmission work. On the contrary, I would even say that working on a smaller car helps you better understand how the engine and transmission work because it gets complicated refinements and other details out of the way.

打个比方，假设你很好奇汽车究竟是如何工作的。如果你对汽车还很陌生，作为学习的一部分，你大概不会一开始就去打造一辆昂贵的法拉利。相反，你可能会先从一辆更小、更简单的车入手，比如大众甲壳虫——即便如此，它也能让你学到很多关于发动机和变速箱的工作原理。事实上，我甚至会说，先从一辆小车开始，反而有助于你更深入地理解发动机和变速箱的运作，因为这样可以避开那些复杂的精巧设计和其他细节，让你专注于核心机制。

While we will use a relatively small model for these educational purposes in this book, the usage, development, and application of the reasoning techniques are still computationally intensive, and later chapters, such as chapters 5-8, will benefit from using a GPU.

尽管在本书中，我们出于教学目的会使用一个相对较小的模型，但推理技术的使用、开发和应用仍然计算密集型。因此，在后续章节（如第5至8章）中，使用GPU将大有裨益。

If you followed the previous section, you should have PyTorch installed, which you can use to see if your computer has a PyTorch-supported GPU by executing the following PyTorch code in Python:

如果您按照前一节的操作进行了设置，应该已经安装了 PyTorch。您可以通过在 Python 中执行以下 PyTorch 代码来检查您的计算机是否配备了 PyTorch 支持的 GPU：

elif torch.xpu.is_available():
    print(f"Intel GPU: {torch.xpu.get_device_name(0)}")
 
elif torch.backends.mps.is_available():
    print("Apple Silicon GPU")
 
else:
    print("Only CPU")

如果你的机器没有GPU来运行代码，也不用担心。第2至5章可以在CPU上以合理的时间完成运行。

根据章节的不同，代码会自动使用 NVIDIA GPU（如果可用）；否则将在 CPU 上运行（或者在推荐使用特定部分或章节时，使用 Apple Silicon GPU）。详细信息将在相应的章节中介绍。

2.4 Preparing input texts for LLMs

2.4 为大语言模型准备输入文本

In this section, we explore how to use a tokenizer to process input and output text for an LLM, as shown in figure 2.5, which expands on the input and output preparation steps shown earlier in figure 2.2 to provide a more detailed view of the tokenization pipeline.

在本节中，我们将探讨如何使用分词器对大语言模型的输入和输出文本进行处理，如图2.5所示。该图在先前图2.2中的输入与输出准备步骤基础上进行了扩展，以更详细地展示分词处理流程。

This matters throughout the rest of the book, because every prompt, reasoning trace, and generated answer ultimately has to be represented as token IDs before the model can process it.

这一点在整本书的后续内容中都至关重要，因为每一个提示、推理轨迹以及模型生成的答案，最终都必须被表示为标记 ID，模型才能对其进行处理。

Figure 2.5 A simplified illustration of how an LLM receives input data and generates output. The user-provided text is tokenized into IDs using the tokenizer's encode method, which are then processed by the LLM to generate output token IDs. These are decoded back into human-readable text using the tokenizer's decode method.
图2.5 语言模型接收输入数据并生成输出的简化示意图。用户提供的文本通过分词器的encode方法被切分为标记ID，随后由语言模型处理，生成输出的标记ID。这些标记ID再通过分词器的decode方法解码为人类可读的文本。

To see how this works in practice, we will begin by loading a tokenizer from this book's reasoning-from-scratch Python package, which should have been installed according to the instructions in section 2.2.

为了了解其实际运作方式，我们首先将从本书的“从零开始推理”Python软件包中加载一个分词器。该软件包应已按照第2.2节中的说明完成安装。

To download the tokenizer files (corresponding to the Qwen3 0.6B base LLM, which we will introduce in the next section), run:

要下载分词器文件（对应于 Qwen3 0.6B 基础大模型，我们将在下一节介绍），请运行：

from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import download_qwen3_small
download_qwen3_small(kind="base", tokenizer_only=True, out_dir="qwen3")
from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import download_qwen3_small download_qwen3_small(kind="base", tokenizer_only=True, out_dir="qwen3")

This will display a progress bar similar to:

这将显示一个类似于以下的进度条：

tokenizer-base.json: 100% (6 MiB / 6 MiB)
分词器基础文件.json：100%（6 MiB / 6 MiB）

The command downloads the tokenizer-base.json file (approximately 6 megabytes in size) and saves it in a qwen3 subdirectory.

该命令会下载 tokenizer-base.json 文件（大小约为 6 MB），并将其保存到 qwen3 子目录中。

Now, we can load the tokenizer settings from the tokenizer file into the Qwen3Tokenizer:

现在，我们可以将分词器文件中的分词器设置加载到 Qwen3Tokenizer 中：

from pathlib import Path
from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import Qwen3Tokenizer
 
tokenizer_path = Path("qwen3") / "tokenizer-base.json"
tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path)
from pathlib import Path from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import Qwen3Tokenizer tokenizer_path = Path("qwen3") / "tokenizer-base.json" tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path)

Since we have not loaded the LLM yet (the central component shown in figure 2.5), we will first do a simpler dry run using just the tokenizer. Specifically, we will do a tokenization round-trip, that is, we will encode a text into token IDs and then decode those IDs back into text, as illustrated in figure 2.6.

由于我们尚未加载大语言模型（如图2.5所示的核心组件），我们将先仅使用分词器进行一次更简单的试运行。具体来说，我们将执行一次分词往返操作：首先将文本编码为标记ID，然后再将这些ID解码回文本，如图2.6所示。

Figure 2.6 A demonstration of the round-trip tokenization process using a tokenizer. The user-provided input text is first converted into token IDs using the encode method, and then accurately reconstructed back into the original text using the decode method.
图2.6 使用分词器演示的往返分词过程。用户提供的输入文本首先通过encode方法转换为标记ID，然后再通过decode方法准确地还原为原始文本。

The following code snippet implements the encoding process shown at the bottom of figure 2.6:

以下代码片段实现了图2.6底部所示的编码过程：

prompt = "Explain large language models."
input_token_ids_list = tokenizer.encode(prompt)
prompt = "解释大型语言模型。" input_token_ids_list = tokenizer.encode(prompt)

And the following code implements the decoding process, converting the token IDs back into text, shown at the top of figure 2.6:

而以下代码实现了解码过程，将标记 ID 转换回文本，如图 2.6 的顶部所示：

text = tokenizer.decode(input_token_ids_list)
print(text)
文本 = 分词器.decode(输入标记ID列表) print(文本)

Based on the printed results, we can see that the tokenizer reconstructed the original input prompt from the token IDs:

从打印结果可以看出，分词器已根据标记 ID 重建了原始输入提示：

'Explain large language models.'
解释大型语言模型。

Before we move on to the LLM, let's take a look at the token IDs that were generated by the encode method. The following code prints each token ID and its corresponding decoded string to help illustrate how the tokenizer works:

在进入大语言模型之前，让我们先来看看由 encode 方法生成的标记 ID。以下代码会打印每个标记 ID 及其对应的解码字符串，以帮助说明分词器的工作原理：

for i in input_token_ids_list:
    print(f"{i} --> {tokenizer.decode([i])}")
对于 input_token_ids_list 中的每个 i： 打印 f"{i} --> {tokenizer.decode([i])}"

The output is as follows:

输出如下：

840 --> Ex
20772 --> plain
3460 -->  large
4128 -->  language
4119 -->  models
13 --> .
840 --> 外星人 20772 --> 普通 3460 --> 大型 4128 --> 语言 4119 --> 模型 13 --> 。

As shown in the output, the original text is split into six token IDs. Each token represents a word or subword, depending on how the tokenizer segments the input.

如输出所示，原始文本被拆分为六个标记 ID。每个标记代表一个词或子词，具体取决于分词器对输入的切分方式。

For example, "Explain" was split into two separate tokens, "Ex" and "plain". This is because the tokenizer algorithm uses a subword-based method based on Byte Pair Encoding (BPE). BPE can represent both common and rare words using a mix of full words and subword units. Spaces are also often included in tokens (for example, " large"), which helps the LLM detect word boundaries.

例如，“Explain”被拆分成了两个独立的标记：“Ex”和“plain”。这是因为分词算法采用了基于字节对编码（BPE）的子词分割方法。BPE能够通过混合使用完整词和子词单元来表示常见词和罕见词。此外，标记中通常还会包含空格（例如，“ large”），这有助于大语言模型识别词边界。

The Qwen3Tokenizer has a vocabulary of about 151,000 tokens, which is considered relatively large as of this writing (for comparison, the early GPT-2 has a vocabulary size of approximately 50,000 tokens, and Llama 3 has a vocabulary size of approximately 128,000 tokens).

Qwen3分词器的词汇表约有151,000个词元，就目前而言，这被认为是一个相对较大的规模（作为对比，早期的GPT-2词汇表大小约为50,000个词元，而Llama 3的词汇表大小约为128,000个词元）。

A larger vocabulary in a language model increases model size because the embedding and output layers must store more token representations, and it can also increase the per-token compute cost of producing the next-token probabilities. A larger vocabulary also allows more words to be represented as single tokens rather than being split into subword components. This can reduce sequence length. For example, splitting a word like "Explain" into "Ex" and "plain" results in more input tokens. More tokens lead to longer input sequences, which increases processing time and resource usage. So the tradeoff is between a larger vocabulary with somewhat higher per-token cost and a smaller vocabulary that often produces longer token sequences. For instance, doubling the number of tokens in a sequence can roughly double the computational cost of running the model, since the model has to process and generate more tokens overall.

语言模型中的词汇表越大，模型规模就会越大，这是因为嵌入层和输出层需要存储更多的词元表示；同时，计算下一个词元概率时的每词元计算开销也会增加。更大的词汇表还允许更多词语以单个词元的形式表示，而不必拆分成子词单元，从而缩短序列长度。例如，将“Explain”拆分为“Ex”和“plain”，就会产生更多的输入词元。而更多的词元会导致输入序列变长，进而增加处理时间和资源消耗。因此，这里存在一种权衡：使用较大的词汇表会带来稍高的每词元成本，而较小的词汇表则往往会产生更长的词元序列。举例来说，如果序列中的词元数量翻倍，运行该模型的计算开销大致也会翻倍，因为模型需要整体处理和生成更多的词元。

Unfortunately, a detailed coverage and from-scratch implementation of a tokenizer is outside the scope of this book. Interested readers can find additional resources, including my from-scratch implementation, in the further resources and reading sections in appendix A.

遗憾的是，对分词器的详细讲解及从零开始的实现超出了本书的范围。感兴趣的读者可以在附录A的“更多资源与推荐阅读”部分找到相关资料，其中包括我编写的从零开始的实现。

Exercise 2.1: Encoding unknown words
练习 2.1：编码未知词

Experiment with the tokenizer to see if and how it handles unknown words. For this, get creative and make up words that don't exist. Also, if you speak multiple languages, try to encode words in a different language than English.

尝试使用分词器，看看它是否以及如何处理未知词。为此，可以发挥创意，编造一些不存在的词汇。此外，如果你会多种语言，也可以试着用非英语的语言来编码单词。

2.5 Loading pre-trained models

2.5 加载预训练模型

In the previous section, we loaded and familiarized ourselves with the tokenizer that prepares the input data for an LLM and converts LLM outputs back into a human-readable text representation. In this section, we will load the LLM itself, as shown in the overview in figure 2.7.

在上一节中，我们加载并熟悉了分词器，它负责为大语言模型准备输入数据，并将模型的输出转换回人类可读的文本表示。在这一节中，我们将加载大语言模型本身，如图2.7所示的概览所示。

Once this base model is in place, the later chapters will build directly on top of it by evaluating it, prompting it in different ways, and eventually training it into a stronger reasoning model.

一旦这个基础模型搭建完毕，后续各章将直接在此基础上展开：对其进行评估、以不同方式引导输入，并最终通过训练将其打造为更强的推理模型。

Figure 2.7 An overview of the four key stages in developing a reasoning model in this book. This section focuses on loading pre-trained LLM in Stage 1.
图2.7 本书中构建推理模型的四个关键阶段概览。本节重点介绍阶段1中的预训练大语言模型加载。

As mentioned previously, this book uses Qwen3 0.6B as a pre-trained base model. In this section, we load its pre-trained weights, as shown in figure 2.7. The "0.6B" in the model name indicates that the model contains approximately 0.6 billion weight parameters.

如前所述，本书使用Qwen3 0.6B作为预训练基础模型。在本节中，我们加载该模型的预训练权重，如图2.7所示。“0.6B”表示该模型约有0.6亿个权重参数。

Why Qwen3? After carefully evaluating several open-weight base models, I chose Qwen3 0.6B for the following reasons:

为什么选择Qwen3？在仔细评估了多个开源基础模型后，我选择了Qwen3 0.6B，原因如下：

  • For this book, we want a small yet capable open-weight model (open-weight models are models whose trained weights are publicly downloadable) that can run on consumer hardware.
  • 对于本书，我们希望选用一个规模较小但功能强大的开放权重模型（开放权重模型是指其训练好的权重可公开下载的模型），并且能够在消费级硬件上运行。
  • Qwen3 offers both a base model (the focus of our reasoning model development) and an official reasoning variant that we can use as a reference for evaluation purposes.
  • Qwen3 提供一个基础模型（这是我们推理模型开发的重点）以及一个官方的推理版本，后者可作为评估参考。
Note
注意

The canonical spelling of "Qwen3" does not include whitespace, whereas, for example, "Llama 3" does.

“Qwen3”的规范拼写不包含空格，而例如“Llama 3”则包含空格。

In line with the spirit of building things "from scratch," this book uses a custom reimplementation of Qwen3 that I wrote in pure PyTorch, which is entirely independent of external LLM libraries. The emphasis of this reimplementation is on code readability and tweakability, in case you want to modify it later for your own experiments. Despite being built from scratch, this implementation remains fully compatible with the original pre-trained Qwen3 model weights.

秉承“从零开始”构建的精神，本书采用我用纯 PyTorch 重新实现的 Qwen3 版本，该实现完全独立于外部的大模型库。此次重写着重于代码的可读性和可调性，以便您日后根据自己的实验需求对其进行修改。尽管是完全从零构建，这一实现仍与原始预训练的 Qwen3 模型权重完全兼容。

This book does not cover the Qwen3 code implementation in depth. This topic alone would fill an entire separate book, similar to my other book, Build A Large Language Model (From Scratch). Instead, this Build A Reasoning Model (From Scratch) book specifically focuses on implementing reasoning methods on top of a base model, in this case, Qwen3.

本书不会深入探讨通义千问3的代码实现。仅这一主题就足以写成一本独立的书籍，类似于我之前的《从零开始构建大型语言模型》。相反，本书《从零开始构建推理模型》专门聚焦于如何在基础模型之上实现推理方法，在本例中，基础模型即通义千问3。

Note
注意

This reimplemented Qwen3 LLM runs entirely locally, just like any other neural network implemented in PyTorch. There are no server-side components or external API calls involved. All model usage happens on your own machine, and your data stays on your device. If you are concerned about privacy, the setup we are using ensures full control over both the LLM inputs and outputs.

这个重新实现的Qwen3大模型完全在本地运行，就像任何用PyTorch实现的神经网络一样。其中不涉及任何服务器端组件或外部API调用。所有模型的使用都在您的设备上进行，您的数据始终保留在本地。如果您对隐私有所顾虑，我们采用的部署方式能够确保您对大模型的输入和输出拥有完全的控制权。

For those interested in additional details about Qwen3, as well as the model code, please see appendix C.

对于有兴趣了解Qwen3更多细节及模型代码的读者，请参阅附录C。

Before we load the model, we can specify the device we are going to use, namely, CPU or GPU. The following code in listing 2.1 will select the best-available device automatically:

在加载模型之前，我们可以指定要使用的设备，即 CPU 或 GPU。清单 2.1 中的以下代码会自动选择当前可用的最佳设备：

Listing 2.1 Get device automatically
def get_device(enable_tensor_cores=True):
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        device = torch.device("cuda")
        print("Using NVIDIA CUDA GPU")
        
        if enable_tensor_cores:
            major, minor = map(int, torch.__version__.split(".")[:2])
            if (major, minor) >= (2, 9):
                torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = "tf32"
                torch.backends.cudnn.conv.fp32_precision = "tf32"
            else:
                torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True
                torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = True
 
    elif torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        device = torch.device("mps")
        print("Using Apple Silicon GPU (MPS)")
 
    elif torch.xpu.is_available():
        device = torch.device("xpu")
        print("Using Intel GPU")
 
    else:
        device = torch.device("cpu")
        print("Using CPU")
 
    return device
def get_device(enable_tensor_cores=True): if torch.cuda.is_available(): device = torch.device("cuda") print("使用 NVIDIA CUDA 显卡") if enable_tensor_cores: major, minor = map(int, torch.__version__.split(".")[:2]) if (major, minor) >= (2, 9): torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = "tf32" torch.backends.cudnn.conv.fp32_precision = "tf32" else: torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = True elif torch.backends.mps.is_available(): device = torch.device("mps") print("使用 Apple Silicon GPU (MPS)") elif torch.xpu.is_available(): device = torch.device("xpu") print("使用 Intel 显卡") else: device = torch.device("cpu") print("使用 CPU") return device

Note that if you have a modern NVIDIA GPU (based on the Ampere architecture or newer), the get_device() function automatically enables Tensor Cores for faster matrix multiplications when enable_tensor_cores=True. This can slightly change floating-point rounding but does not noticeably affect results in this book, and the speed advantage on newer cards is worth it. On non-NVIDIA devices, these settings are ignored.

请注意，如果你使用的是基于Ampere架构或更高级架构的现代NVIDIA GPU，当`enable_tensor_cores=True`时，`get_device()`函数会自动启用Tensor Core以加速矩阵乘法。这可能会轻微改变浮点数的舍入方式，但在本书中对结果的影响并不明显；而且在较新的显卡上，由此带来的速度优势是值得的。而在非NVIDIA设备上，这些设置将被忽略。

Using the code from listing 2.1, we can then obtain the device as follows:

使用清单2.1中的代码，我们就可以按如下方式获取设备：

device = get_device()
设备 = 获取设备()

While GPUs generally provide substantial speed and performance improvements, it can be helpful to initially run the remaining code in this chapter using the CPU for compatibility and debugging purposes. You can temporarily override the automatic selection by explicitly setting:

虽然 GPU 通常能带来显著的速度和性能提升，但为了兼容性和调试，建议在本章的剩余代码中先使用 CPU 运行。你可以通过显式设置来临时覆盖自动选择：

device = torch.device("cpu")
设备 = 机器学习框架的设备对象（例如，"cpu"）

After finishing the chapter and verifying the code works properly on the CPU, remove or comment out the manual override and rerun the code. If your system has a GPU, you should then observe improved performance.

完成本章内容并在 CPU 上验证代码正常运行后，移除或注释掉手动覆盖代码，然后重新运行程序。如果您的系统配备 GPU，您应该会看到性能提升。

Note
注意

The code in the remainder of this chapter was executed on a Mac Mini with an Apple M4 CPU. Performance comparisons with the Apple Silicon M4 GPU and the NVIDIA H100 GPU are included at the end of the chapter.

本章剩余部分的代码是在搭载苹果M4芯片的Mac Mini上执行的。章节末尾附有苹果自研M4 GPU与NVIDIA H100 GPU的性能对比。

Before we load the model and put it onto the selected device, we first need to download the weights for Qwen3 0.6B. These files are required to initialize the pre-trained model correctly. In the previous section, we called the same function with tokenizer_only=True to download only the tokenizer files. Here, we set tokenizer_only=False so that the model weights are downloaded as well:

在加载模型并将其部署到选定的设备之前，我们首先需要下载通义千问3 0.6B模型的权重文件。这些文件是正确初始化预训练模型所必需的。在上一节中，我们通过将tokenizer_only参数设置为True来仅下载分词器文件。在这里，我们将tokenizer_only设置为False，以便同时下载模型权重：

download_qwen3_small(kind="base", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir="qwen3")
下载Qwen3小型模型（类型为“base”，仅加载分词器设置为False，输出目录为“qwen3”）

The output is as follows:

输出如下：

qwen3-0.6B-base.pth: 100% (1433 MiB / 1433 MiB)
✓ qwen3/tokenizer-base.json already up-to-date
qwen3-0.6B-base.pth：100%（1433 MiB / 1433 MiB） ✓ qwen3/tokenizer-base.json 已是最新

(There is a checkmark in front of the tokenizer because we already downloaded it in the previous section.)

（分词器前面有一个对勾，因为我们已经在上一节中下载了它。）

After downloading the model weights via the previous step, we can now instantiate a Qwen3Model class into which we load the pre-trained weights via PyTorch's load_state_dict method:

在通过上一步下载模型权重后，我们现在可以实例化一个 Qwen3Model 类，并通过 PyTorch 的 load_state_dict 方法加载预训练权重：

from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import Qwen3Model, QWEN_CONFIG_06_B
 
model_path = Path("qwen3") / "qwen3-0.6B-base.pth"
model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)  #A
model.load_state_dict(torch.load(model_path))  #B
model.to(device)  #C
#A Instantiate a Qwen3 model with random weights as placeholders
#B Load the pre-trained weights into the model
#C Transfer the model to the designated device (e.g., "cuda")
#A 实例化一个使用随机权重作为占位符的Qwen3模型 #B 将预训练权重加载到模型中 #C 将模型迁移到指定的设备（例如“cuda”）

Note that if the device setting is "cpu", the model.to(device) operation will be skipped because the model already sits in CPU memory by default.

请注意，如果设备设置为 "cpu"，则会跳过 model.to(device) 操作，因为模型默认就已经位于 CPU 内存中。

After executing the code above, you should see the following output (if you are not running the code in an interactive environment like a Jupyter notebook, you have to run print(model) to see the output):

执行上述代码后，你应该会看到以下输出（如果你不在像 Jupyter Notebook 这样的交互式环境中运行代码，就需要运行 print(model) 才能看到输出）：

  (tok_emb): Embedding(151936, 1024)

        (W_key): Linear(in_features=1024, out_features=1024, bias=False)
        (W_value): Linear(in_features=1024, out_features=1024, bias=False)
        (out_proj): Linear(in_features=2048, out_features=1024, bias=False)
        (q_norm): RMSNorm()
        (k_norm): RMSNorm()
      )
      (ff): FeedForward(
        (fc1): Linear(in_features=1024, out_features=3072, bias=False)
        (fc2): Linear(in_features=1024, out_features=3072, bias=False)
        (fc3): Linear(in_features=3072, out_features=1024, bias=False)
      )

  )
